("Alpha Compute" or the "Company"), a technology pioneer in AI Confidential Compute and GPU-as-a-service (GPUaaS), is proud to serve as a sponsor of the 9/11 & Freedom 250 Gala, a landmark evening hosted by WABC Radio commemorating the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks and celebrating the 250th anniversary of the United States of America.

Hosted by entrepreneurs and philanthropists John and Margo Catsimatidis, the gala honors the courage, sacrifice and resilience of the American people. Proceeds will benefit four organizations dedicated to honoring the legacy of September 11, supporting New York City communities, preserving American history and inspiring future generations through education and service:

"Twenty-five years ago, New York City showed the world what courage and resilience look like. Many of us lost friends, co-workers, and family members. Out of this rubble, came key organizations like Tunnel to Towers Foundation, who have built over 2,000 mortgage-free houses for disabled veterans, and the Police Athletic League, an organization I fondly remember growing up in New York City. We are honored to stand with them," said
Enzo Villani, Executive Chairman and President of Alpha Compute.
Brittany Kaiser, CEO of Alpha Compute

commented, "America's first 250 years were built on infrastructure: canals, railroads, the electric grid, the interstates. The next chapter will be built on compute, and we are proud to be one of the companies building it."
The sponsorship reflects Alpha Compute's ties to New York City and its view that the country's next 250 years will depend, as its first did, on the people who build its infrastructure.
The evening will feature keynote speakers, patriotic tributes and special presentations, and will bring together leaders from business, government, technology and the nonprofit community.
